quotes.text: So think of inventory management as the stock record. Warehouse management turns that record into guided physical work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws a crisp line between inventory management and warehouse management.

quotes.text: Quarantine means the goods remain physically in the building, but workers can't use or ship them as normal stock.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines quarantine stock simply and shows why it protects customer orders.

quotes.text: A location directive is a set of rules that answers, where should this item go now?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reduces a technical setup term to the question it answers.

quotes.text: A barcode scan at the shelf captures the item, location, container, or quantity, while the worker handles it. There is no paper note waiting in a pocket until later.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for recording warehouse work at the point of action.

quotes.text: If the location rules point stock to the wrong area, a scanner will faithfully direct a worker there. If the work steps do not match how the warehouse actually operates, the device can add friction instead of removing it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical warning that warehouse setup quality determines the value of guided work.

takeaways: Inventory management records how much stock the business owns, while Dynamics 365 Warehouse Management knows exactly where it sits and what workers should do with it next.
Location directives, work templates and waves turn warehouse rules into step-by-step tasks that workers confirm with scans on mobile devices.
Because warehouse work runs inside Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, purchasing, sales, production, quality and finance all see the same stock picture.
hook: A spreadsheet can tell you that 50 units exist somewhere, but it cannot guide a worker to the right shelf. This episode explains Dynamics 365 Warehouse Management in plain English for operations teams, consultants and business users. Learn how receiving, put-away, picking, counting and shipping connect to the rest of the business.
